candidates.title: Gucci quietly cut a Padlock bag 30% (EUR 3,500 -> 2,450) and other items; LVMH, which once said 'we're not Coca-Cola', is now discussing cuts; Hermes holds price and grows
candidates.classification: breaking -> emerging (reported 15-17 Nov, Korea follow-up 26 Nov)

sources.claim: Headline: 'Gucci Price Cuts Break Luxury's Biggest Taboo. Louis Vuitton Isn't Following.' Some Gucci prices cut by 30% as middle-class shoppers retreat; cuts surfaced via shoppers, social accounts and Google price flags before any executive comment; Kering frames it as a 'price architecture' reset. Body details read via extraction summary — use only where corroborated.

Padlock Crystal Small handbag: EUR 3,500 in France in July, now EUR 2,450 (-30%), per Bernstein, first reported by the Wall Street Journal. LVMH discussing responses such as price cuts; a year earlier its CFO Cecile Cabanis ruled out price adjustments and said the company 'was not Coca-Cola' (paraphrase, translated). Goldman Sachs estimates Louis Vuitton Q3 sales down 8%.

Same Padlock figures (EUR 3,500 -> 2,450, -30%); 16 new bag styles at $2,000 or less on Gucci's US site. Cabanis quoted (translated): 'We are not Coca-Cola' (a year ago) vs now 'discussing bold and immediate measures, such as price cuts, internally.' LV holding prices out of concern that cuts could damage brand value.

Cuts on selected handbags, footwear and ready-to-wear; new Padlock price is a regular selling price, not a markdown; sneakers EUR 800 -> 560-595; Mercato tote reportedly 20-25% cheaper. Kering Q3 presentation: 'reshaping of product and price architecture, with targeted adjustments to improve perceived value, led by Handbags'. Flag credited to Bernstein's Luca Solca.
Padlock figures (about 30%, per Bernstein's Luca Solca); cuts reported by WSJ; LVMH has not announced a broad price-cutting strategy for Louis Vuitton.

'They said prices would never drop': Gucci, Boucheron, Van Cleef & Arpels cutting Korean prices; Gucci Mercato Small Tote 4.45M -> 3.5M won (~-21%); luxury department-store growth slowed from 40%+ (Q2) to ~10% (Oct); Prada CEO Andrea Guerra: 'The mere fact that pricing is being talked about means there is a problem.'
Gucci Q3 2026 revenue EUR 1.29bn, -4% reported, -6% comparable; retail -9% comparable. Luca de Meo: 'The recovery of Gucci remains our defining priority.'
Hermes Q3 2026 revenue +4.3% at constant rates to EUR 4,096m; leather goods and saddlery +10.8% to EUR 1,912m. (No price statement in this article.)

lenses.verification_red_team: C1: Padlock EUR 3,500 -> 2,450 (France, July -> Nov) agrees across Sedaily, FNNews, Inc., Open, TheIndustry; origin is Bernstein (Luca Solca) / WSJ — attribute as 'reported', Gucci made no announcement and no official Gucci statement on the cuts was found; Kering's own wording: 'targeted adjustments to improve perceived value, led by Handbags' (Q3 presentation, via TheIndustry). Not all Gucci prices fell: say 'some bags, shoes and clothes'. 'We're not Coca-Cola' is LVMH CFO Cecile Cabanis, a year ago, via translated Korean press (FNNews quotes it, Sedaily paraphrases) and Forbes summary — use as 'LVMH's finance chief said, a year ago' and keep the wording exactly 'We're not Coca-Cola'. LV has NOT cut prices: say 'discussing' only. Gucci Q3 -6% comparable (FashionUnited, primary-reported). Hermes leather goods +10.8% Q3 (Ideal Investisseur). Do not claim '13 quarters of decline' (Forbes summary citing WSJ, unread) or Bain customer counts on screen. Do not call it viral.
lenses.audience_psychology: Everyone knows Gucci; everyone has a gut rule that 'luxury never goes on sale'. A 30% cut breaks that rule and triggers two opposite feelings: the would-be buyer ('finally') and the owner ('so mine is worth less'). The Coca-Cola line is a quotable villain line that turns. Persian-speaking viewers know Gucci, LV and Hermes and live with price shocks; business owners face the 'should I discount?' question every week. Share test: 'Gucci cut its bag price 30% and LV's CFO once said we're not Coca-Cola' — yes.
lenses.brand_fit: Pure pricing/communication strategy and positioning: price as a brand signal, discount vs desire. Behnood's voice (strategist with a stance) can take a side: a cut fixes a price problem, not a desire problem. Lesson works for a cafe or a clinic as well as luxury.

gates.brand_fit: C1 pass; C2 pass but repeat-heavy; C3 fail repeat (GTA 11-23); C4 fail freshness/recognition; C5 fail ethics (real person's body); C6 fail repeat; C7 fail recognition; C8 fail verification; C9/C10/C12 fail freshness; C11 fail rotation.
gates.story: C1 tension: 'In luxury the price IS the product. Gucci cut it 30%; Hermes kept its prices and its leather goods grew 10.8%.' Concrete image: a padlock (the bag's name) hanging from a price tag with the old price crossed out. Conflict: Gucci cuts vs LV 'we're not Coca-Cola' vs Hermes holds.

winner.why: Highest on both rubrics (README 86, stage 86, estimates), global famous brand with a clear rule-break, three-brand conflict, concrete object (Padlock), every on-screen claim sourced from 2+ outlets, and a lesson every business owner can use. Runner-up C2 (Coca-Cola two Christmases) held back for AI-topic fatigue.
